content.user_title: Build Azure AI Projects Apps in Python
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable guidance for Azure AI Projects SDK workflows. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code work with clients, agents, tools, evaluations, and Foundry resources.
actual_capabilities: Create AIProjectClient examples for Azure AI Foundry projects.
Show native Foundry agent creation, versioning, threads, messages, and runs.
Explain OpenAI-compatible client usage inside an Azure AI Projects app.
Outline connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, memory stores, and evaluations.
Compare azure-ai-projects with azure-ai-agents for SDK selection.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure AI Foundry project and endpoint.
Code examples need project-specific resource names, models, and credentials.
Does not replace Azure IAM, networking, or deployment security review.
Reference files mentioned by the guide are not present in the scanned package.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Foundry app
use_cases.description: Use SDK examples to connect a Python app to an Azure AI Foundry project.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent workflows
use_cases.description: Plan agent creation, versioning, tools, threads, messages, and runs for a team.

use_cases.title: Prepare evaluation flows
use_cases.description: Map OpenAI-compatible evaluation runs and built-in criteria for quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a project client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the basic steps to connect AIProjectClient to my Azure AI Foundry project using environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a Foundry agent with a model deployment, clear instructions, and a simple thread and run flow.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a client style
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare native AIProjectClient operations with the OpenAI-compatible client for my Python application. Recommend when to use each.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production workflow for versioned agents, connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, memory stores, and evaluations in Azure AI Projects.

output_examples.input: I need a first Azure AI Projects app.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist with required packages, environment variables, authentication, client creation, and a first agent run.

output_examples.input: I need to choose between azure-ai-projects and azure-ai-agents.
output_examples.output: A comparison that favors azure-ai-projects for Foundry integration and azure-ai-agents for lower-level agent apps.

output_examples.input: I need an evaluation plan for an agent.
output_examples.output: An evaluation outline with test items, criteria, run naming, and follow-up review steps.

best_practices: Store endpoint and model deployment values in environment variables or secure configuration.
Use versioned agents for production changes and record model deployment names.
Review tool access before enabling file search, code interpreter, web, OpenAPI, or MCP tools.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding real project endpoints, deployment names, or credentials in shared prompts.
Enabling powerful agent tools without reviewing data access and execution boundaries.
Using the OpenAI-compatible client when native Foundry resource operations are required.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Python apps with Azure AI Projects, including Foundry clients, agents, tools, evaluations, and project resources.

faq.question: Does it run Azure commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. The scanned file is documentation with examples. Users decide which commands or SDK calls to run.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include real Azure credentials?
faq.answer: No. It uses placeholder endpoints and environment variable names for configuration.

faq.question: When should I use azure-ai-projects instead of azure-ai-agents?
faq.answer: Use azure-ai-projects for high-level Foundry integration, versioning, connections, deployments, datasets, indexes, and evaluations.

faq.question: What should I prepare before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare an Azure AI Foundry project endpoint, a model deployment name, and appropriate Azure credentials.
